correctness.rationale: The six-state four-site generator built independently from allowed hops is irreducible for positive rates and |epsilon|<1. Solving its stationary perturbation equations through order two and applying the signed hop functional divided by four confirms the general factorization symbolically. For (2,3,4,t) the cubic bracket becomes -12(t-2)(t-11), S=9t+26, and S+ac+bd=2(6t+17), giving the three positive zeros stated. The t=3 equality is a reflection; the repeated adjacent rate at t=2 does not give a reflection because the two other rates differ, and all four rates differ at t=11. An independent normalized stationary solve at t=11 verifies the rational current and its even part. The bound E>=44850>688>=|O| and the sign of the even numerator show positivity at all 0<|epsilon|<1, with the stated quartic Taylor coefficient. This is quartic leading response of the even part, not of the full current. Particle conservation makes the bond current constant over the ring at stationarity. A direct three-state computation confirms the odd one-particle and one-vacancy currents for length three; the other two sectors have no jumps. This verifies the minimum length among lengths at least three. The frozen verifier was inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: The cubic factor gives a testable, exact cancellation locus beyond opposite-site equalities for arbitrary positive rates in the smallest nontrivial interacting sector. The t=11 solution demonstrates that a zero on that locus need not produce odd current, with a sign-definite even part on the entire open bias interval. This is more than replacing one known witness by another and does not require credit for first finding the phenomenon.
